title: an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands
intention: Every intention that owns a boat declares which hands its owner-gate admits, machine-readably, so the Law 6 check at a gated crossing works for the whole fleet rather than for the one charter that needed it first — and the question of who may MINT on an intention's behalf, as distinct from who may act for it, gets an answer instead of a flat capability.
why: The parent voyage (boat-owner-is-read-not-stated) made the boat's owner READ rather than stated, which required an intention to say something a gate can stand on. It gave harbor_master's charter a `gated_by` list and deliberately stopped there: filling 24 charters in one pass would be a back-fill of values nobody checked, which is exactly what that voyage refused to do to 100 tickets. The consequence is real and is the cost this ticket carries — every OTHER component's first forward crossing into PROVED now refuses until its charter gains the field, with the refusal naming the file and the one-line fix. That is grow-against-need working as designed, and it is also a tax on voyages that have nothing to do with the parent ticket. Whether the refusal-with-a-fix is enough mitigation is a claim, not a fact, so it is watched rather than asserted.
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; the owner alone gates writes, and delegated access happens only through the owner's gate, never ambiently) and Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — prose in an `owner` field cannot gate, which is what the measurement below establishes).

falsifier.proves_green: PROOF GATE (tester, Law 8): proofs beside the code at the address that changes — for the fleet-wide half that is wherever the read lives (cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py today); teeth a hollow build could not pass are (i) an actor that is a SUBSTRING or SUPERSTRING of an admitted one is refused, which is the failure mode the prose `owner` field would have had, and (ii) a charter lacking the field refuses with that charter's path in the message rather than falling back. BUILD GATE: build_inspector over the changed component at the PROVEME crossing. FEEDBACK TO ORIGIN ON FAILURE (Law 3 + CP2): a red routes back to this ticket and to the parent's probe, not to a private fix. RUN TWICE, never trust the first green. NON-HOLLOW METHOD: the vocabulary half is proved by pointing the check at the 4 records spelling the actor 'claude' — if it admits them the vocabulary was settled, if it refuses them the ticket has found its own first real case.
falsifier.proves_red: FALSIFIER — RED on any of: (1) the fleet-wide fill is done by writing the same list into 24 charters in one pass, which would be a back-fill of values nobody checked, the exact thing the parent voyage refused to do to 100 tickets; (2) `gated_by` grows into a role or permission system (wildcards, groups, inheritance) — it is a list of hands, and anything richer is a registry with a new name, which this system frowns on; (3) the minting question is answered by adding a second list beside the first without a measured case that needed the distinction; (4) an intention ends up declaring hands for a boat it does not own. HORIZON: the first crossing on this box by an actor that is NOT the single hand — a second device, or Akien acting directly. Until then the fleet-wide question is untestable in the way that matters, and this ticket says so rather than sailing on n=1. Note the horizon is shared with the parent ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated and with its probe: one event answers both, which is why this is filed rather than built now.
falsifier.horizon: the first crossing on this box by an actor that is NOT the single hand — a second device, or Akien acting directly. Shared with the parent ticket and with its probe: one event answers both.

children: none, because both halves share one horizon (the first crossing by a hand that is not this box's single hand) and neither can prove before the other on the evidence available — splitting them would produce two tickets waiting on the same event, which is a decomposition that buys nothing. The parent ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated is at CairnCommons/tickets/boat-owner-is-read-not-stated.json and is where the shape being extended was built.

questions.a: TWO ARE LOAD-BEARING AND BOTH ARE NAMED RATHER THAN DISCHARGED. (1) That `gated_by` — a list of actor-name strings on a charter — is the right shape fleet-wide, not just for harbor_master. It was chosen against a measurement (22 of 24 beside-code charters carry an `owner` over 60 characters and 2 carry an EMPTY one, so matching an actor against that prose is a substring scan that goes green for the wrong reason), but a shape that works at n=1 is not thereby proven at n=24; homeless intentions in intentions-not-beside-code/ have never been asked the question at all. (2) That an actor VOCABULARY exists to put in the list. It does not: the corpus already carries two spellings for one mover, `CC` x12 and `claude` x4 in the actor field, because nothing has ever gated it. An exact-membership check over an unsettled vocabulary refuses on a spelling, and this ticket cannot be finished without settling it or explicitly deciding to accept both.

ONE POINT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRAPPED AND IT IS THE SECOND HALF OF THIS TICKET: who may MINT on an intention's behalf, as distinct from who may act for it. The parent voyage closed the direct hole (mint_grant now reads the boat and refuses a minter that is not an admitted hand), which means any admitted hand may now mint for any other hand — a flat capability where the design may want a narrower one. That is unwrapped on purpose: it cannot be reasoned out on a box with one hand, because every arrangement is observationally identical there. Also unwrapped, and smaller: whether a boat already BERTHED in port (a component with a history but no live ticket file) resolves an owner at all. Anticipated as a shape during the parent's chart, never observed.

CHECKED AGAINST THREE, NO EXCLUSIVE-AND-TERMINAL CONFLICT FOUND. (a) Law 6 (one owner, gated writes, no ambient delegation) — this ticket IMPLEMENTS the second clause rather than competing with it; the distinction to record is that membership in `gated_by` is delegation AT REST, recorded in the charter, while a Grant is delegation PER OPERATION, and Cairn now has both. (b) 'no enforcer — gated ownership' and the standing dislike of registries: a per-intention list on the intention's own charter is the anti-registry shape by construction (the fact lives at its subject's address, Law 5), whereas one central table of who-may-move-what would be the collision — so the shape is the point, and clause (2) of the falsifier is what keeps it. (c) decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal — no conflict; this ticket extends its chain (intention -> ticket -> workflow -> boat) to the 23 intentions the parent voyage deliberately left alone.

OBSERVATION FED TO THE WATCH, 2026-08-15 (first second-hand fill event): the intentions_model_compiler's PROVED crossing (ticket the-present-tense-corpus-rewrites-once) refused OwnerUnresolvable exactly as this ticket's why predicts; the charter gained gated_by ['CC'] derived from its owner prose per base's stated rule, and the fix was one line with the refusal naming it. The mitigation held — but the fill was made by CC under refusal-pressure mid-crossing, RATIFICATION NOT SOUGHT, which is the minting-half question this ticket flags at Akien's gate showing up in the wild. Score so far: 1 fill event, 1 one-line fix, 0 ratified.

how: Add gated_hands field to intention+why.json schema — which hands the owner-gate admits, machine-readably. Build the Law 6 check at gated crossings to read it.
links: cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py — twice: in `gated_by_why` on the charter and in mint_grant's docstring, so the code that leaves the hole standing points at the ticket that owns it rather than explaining it in prose.

cairn/tools/import_sieve/intention+why.json and cairn/machines/build_inspector/intention+why.json — filled 2026-08-12 during ticket reachability-replaces-the-allowlist, which would have refused at the clearance gate with OwnerUnresolvable at its own last step. Both derive ["CC"] from their `owner` prose by the rule cairn/tools/base's gated_by_why states, and both cite this ticket for what they do NOT settle. The fill count moves 3 -> 5 of 24 beside-code charters, and it moved the way this ticket asked it to: at a crossing that demanded it, not by a sweep.

A MEASURED INCONSISTENCY IN THE EXISTING FILLS, found while deriving the two above and recorded here rather than silently matched. cairn/tools/base and cairn/devices/harbor_master both derive gated_by from their `owner` prose and say so in a `gated_by_why`. cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop carries ["Akien", "CC"] with NO `gated_by_why`, while its `owner` names only CC as write-gater — so it does not follow the stated rule. That entry is CC's, added 2026-08-12 in cairn commit dc3634f during a-record-reaches-disk. THE QUESTION IT RAISES IS THIS TICKET'S: does Law 9 put Akien in EVERY gated_by regardless of the `owner` prose, or only where the prose puts him? base's own why argues the first for base specifically ('a gate on base's own charter that could refuse him would be a translation of the spec refusing the spec'); harbor_master deliberately argues the second. Two of the three fills cannot both be the general rule. Until it is answered, the derivation-from-prose rule is what the new fills follow, because it is the one that is written down.
priority: after the parent's horizon, or at the first crossing by a component whose charter lacks the field — whichever comes first — It cannot be proved before its horizon (on a one-hand box every arrangement of the minting question is observationally identical), and it becomes urgent the moment a second component tries to cross into PROVED — which is a real, dated event rather than a preference.
